title: 5 best AI image expanders in 2027: uncrop without stretching
summary: Compare Magic Hour, Photoshop, Canva, Pixelcut and Photoroom for image outpainting. Choose by canvas controls, exports, commercial use and workflow.
body_markdown:
## Quick answer


**Start with Magic Hour for a browser expansion with independent side padding; choose Photoshop for layered cleanup, Canva for finished designs, Pixelcut for a simple uncrop workflow, or Photoroom for product catalogs.**


All five generate new surroundings beyond an image’s edges. The right choice depends on the space you need, the cleanup you expect, and the file and usage permissions required for the finished image.


A tightly cropped product photo can still become a useful banner. The decision is whether to generate extra scene content, crop what you have, or place the image on a larger plain background. This guide compares actual expansion workflows so you can choose before paying for retries or moving a project between editors.


Magic Hour publishes this guide and makes one of the tools below. We checked official product documentation and usage terms on October 14, 2026. The best-for recommendations are editorial judgments about workflow fit, not results from a shared-input quality or speed test.

## What an AI image expander does


An **AI image expander** adds generated content outside the original image boundary. Image extender, outpainting and uncrop describe this same basic job. Cropping removes content to change composition; stretching changes proportions; upscaling adds pixel dimensions to a composition. Pick expansion when keeping the visible subject matters more than keeping the original frame.


For example, a square product photo may need open space on the left for ad copy. Expanding only that side can make the layout work without cutting into the product. A photo that only needs a larger export belongs in an[image upscaler](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-image-upscalers) , while an unwanted object inside the frame calls for an edit or fill workflow.


The added surroundings are inferred, not recovered from a hidden original photograph. For an interior, that means a newly generated doorway is a design suggestion, not proof that the property has one. Keep an untouched source and decide which visible details must remain factual before expanding.


## How we compare these tools


The shortlist separates documented controls from the result you must evaluate on your own image. We used five buyer criteria. They also form a repeatable acceptance sheet for comparing two tools without relying on different vendor demo images.


**Canvas control:** record source dimensions, target width-to-height ratio and which of the four sides must grow. A centered expansion and a left-only expansion solve different layout problems.


**Subject preservation:** list the product label, face, garment pattern or architectural feature that must stay faithful. Compare those regions with the original rather than judging only the new background.


**Boundary quality:** inspect at 100% zoom where original and generated areas meet. Count visible seams, repeated objects and broken straight lines; also review the complete composition at its delivery size.


**Delivered file:** open the downloaded image and record its pixel dimensions, file type and watermark state. A large preview or large upload limit does not establish the dimensions of the export.


**Cost of a usable result:** track paid generations, export usage and cleanup time for the image you approve. A low entry price is less useful if the required file remains locked behind a different plan.


No numerical quality ratings are assigned here. For broader editing choices after expansion, see our[AI image editor comparison](https://magichour.ai/blog/the-best-ai-image-editors) .


## The five image expanders and when to choose each


### 1. Magic Hour — best for independent padding and a connected browser workflow


Choose[Magic Hour AI Image Expander](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-image-expander) when you want to make room around an existing image with a preset ratio or independently controlled sides. This fits a product hero with copy on one side, a wider landscape composition, or a portrait that needs more breathing room. The public product route offers a free trial without signup and advertises watermark-free results.


The[full Image Expander editor](https://magichour.ai/create/ai-image-expander) adds an optional prompt. Leave it empty for a continuation, or describe the surroundings you want. The important first step is still selecting an expansion: in Custom, at least one side must extend beyond the source. A prompt alone does not make an unchanged canvas larger. The[official guide](https://help.magichour.ai/en/articles/16917119-ai-image-expander-step-by-step-guide) explains the ratio, padding and generation flow.


Magic Hour public guest canvas after a sample upload, captured October 14, 2026. The screenshot shows framing controls; generation was not submitted.[Open the live Image Expander](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-image-expander) .


**Best workflow:** select the destination layout, expand only the space it needs, inspect the new edges, and then move the approved still into the next creation step. If the final piece is a moving ad, the completed image can become an input to[Image-to-Video](https://magichour.ai/products/image-to-video) . Expansion itself does not animate the photograph.


**Know before paying:** a watermark-free trial is separate from commercial permission. Magic Hour’s[Terms](https://magichour.ai/terms-of-service) permit commercial use for paid subscribers, credit-pack customers and separately agreed paid usage-based arrangements; outputs created without a paid arrangement are personal-use only. Review the editor’s resolution and credit estimate for the selected job. We would choose Photoshop instead when the handoff requires an editable layered retouching file.


### 2. Photoshop Generative Expand — best for layered editing and precise cleanup


Choose Photoshop when the expansion is one part of a larger retouching job. Adobe’s[Generative Expand tutorial](https://www.adobe.com/learn/photoshop/web/the-unlock-how-to-quickly-expand-an-image) starts with the Crop tool: enlarge the canvas, generate the missing surroundings, and select a variation. Its workflow keeps access to generated variations through the generative layer, so you can revisit that choice while refining the document.


Adobe’s[reframing lesson](https://www.adobe.com/learn/photoshop/web/firefly-photographers-reframe-photos-with-ai) also demonstrates positioning the subject inside a new aspect ratio instead of accepting a centered composition. That makes the workflow useful when a designer needs both extra scene area and a deliberate subject position.


**Best workflow:** decide the crop boundary, generate the expansion, then review it alongside the rest of your document. Keep the editable project before exporting a flattened image. This is a stronger fit than a quick standalone uncrop when the deliverable still needs retouching, compositing or later client revisions.


**Know before paying:** Adobe’s[credit rules](https://helpx.adobe.com/creative-cloud/apps/generative-ai/generative-credits-faq.html) vary by plan, feature and model. Do not assume every Photoshop account has the same unlimited generation entitlement. For Firefly outputs, Adobe’s[FAQ](https://helpx.adobe.com/firefly/web/get-started/learn-the-basics/adobe-firefly-faq.html) allows commercial projects for non-beta features, with stated conditions for beta features. That is not a blanket statement about every partner model or source asset. If you only need one reframed image, a browser tool may be a lighter starting point than a full editing workflow.


### 3. Canva Magic Expand — best for finishing the design in the same workspace


Choose Canva when the image needs to become a designed asset: a social post, slide, campaign banner or layout with text and graphics.[Magic Expand](https://www.canva.com/help/using-magic-expand/) is available within the photo-editing workflow: select the photo, open Edit, find the tool, choose a size or drag a handle beyond the border, then expand.


The key advantage for this job is the destination. You are already working inside a design, so the expanded background can provide space for the headline, logo and layout elements that belong around it.


**Know the export step:** Canva’s Help Center says an expanded image can be downloaded separately only when it is downloaded as part of a design. It also flags faces, hands and transparent backgrounds as cases that may not work well. If a colleague expects an isolated image file, check the completed design download early rather than discovering that difference at handoff.


**Know before paying:** Canva’s[product page](https://www.canva.com/features/ai-image-expander/) and[AI-access guidance](https://www.canva.com/help/ai-access/) describe plan-dependent feature access and changing allowances. Check the control and allowance on your own account; this guide does not promise an identical free quota to every reader. Its[AI Product Terms](https://www.canva.com/policies/ai-product-terms/) also distinguish your own inputs from Canva library content incorporated into an output. Expanding a library photo does not remove the original content license. Choose a standalone browser expander if you mainly want a downloaded image with no design project around it.


### 4. Pixelcut Uncrop — best for a direct upload-and-expand workflow


Choose[Pixelcut Uncrop](https://www.pixelcut.ai/uncrop) when the task is straightforward: upload a photo, adjust the canvas, generate a continuation and download. Its current tool page lists JPG, PNG and HEIC inputs, with a 50 MB and 6000 × 6000-pixel input limit. Those are upload limits, not a promise that every result downloads at that size.


The documented controls let you choose a preset aspect ratio or extend the canvas in a direction, and regenerate to explore alternatives. This makes it a useful shortlist option for someone who wants to compare a plain uncrop flow with Magic Hour’s side-padding workflow. Pixelcut’s page advertises a free HD download without a watermark; verify the file you actually receive for the intended placement.


**Best workflow:** take a source that already has the right subject, choose the required frame and inspect the edge continuation. Keep headline and logo text as separate design elements afterwards. That makes it easier to revise the composition without asking a generator to reproduce exact typography.


**Know before paying:** Pixelcut’s[pricing page](https://www.pixelcut.ai/pricing) labels free Expand Image access as limited and lists commercial licensing on paid plans. Its[commercial-use help](https://help.pixelcut.ai/article/39-commercial-use) also requires appropriate rights to imported content. We do not interpret a free download as an unlimited production or universal commercial-use entitlement. Check the selected plan and export before committing a batch of client assets. For complex retouching with a layered handoff, Photoshop remains the more appropriate workflow in this shortlist.


### 5. Photoroom AI Expand — best for product-image and catalog workflows


Choose[Photoroom AI Expand](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/ai-expand) when the subject is a product and the same image must fit several listing or campaign formats. The official workflow uploads the product photo, chooses new dimensions through Resize, and generates additional scene area around it. Photoroom also documents carrying target dimensions into batch or API workflows, which is relevant when the job extends beyond one banner.


There is an important difference between changing canvas size and actually generating the background. In[Photoroom’s resizing guidance](https://help.photoroom.com/en/articles/9925607-troubleshooting-ai-resizing) , a simple empty, transparent or single-color background can result in a larger canvas without a newly generated scene. For an imported photo, preserving the original photographic background as part of the design matters. Diagnose the background layer before treating an unchanged result as a generation failure.


**Best workflow:** approve the framing and product accuracy on one representative image before applying a target format across a catalog. Check the silhouette, package label, contact shadow and repeated surface details; format consistency alone does not establish product fidelity. For a broader product-photo workflow, compare our[AI product photo editors](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-photo-editors-for-product-photography) .


**Know before paying:** the current[pricing page](https://www.photoroom.com/pricing) includes AI Expand/Resize as a core paid-plan tool without an AI-credit charge, subject to fair use, while exports have separate allowances. Included expansion does not mean unlimited exports. Photoroom’s[commercial-use guidance](https://help.photoroom.com/en/articles/12523455-free-accounts-and-commercial-use) limits free accounts to personal use. Use the current plan screen for your intended commercial workflow instead of relying on an older unlimited-export description.

## A worked example: turn a portrait product shot into a 16:9 banner


**This is a layout calculation and reusable brief, not a measured generation result.** Suppose the source is 1200 × 1800 pixels. Keeping the full source height for a 16:9 layout gives a target canvas 3200 pixels wide: 1800 × 16 ÷ 9 = 3200. That leaves 2000 pixels of extra horizontal space to plan.


A centered layout adds 1000 pixels on each side. If the campaign needs copy on the left, the same plan could use 1500 pixels on the left and 500 on the right. The original source then sits farther right in the composition. The tool’s export resolution may differ from this planning canvas, so confirm the downloaded file instead of assuming these are supported output dimensions.


In this example, 62.5% of the planned canvas lies outside the source: (3200 − 1200) ÷ 3200. A large expansion therefore asks the model to invent most of the surrounding scene. If that scene becomes distracting or inconsistent, reduce the added area, use a plain design background, or choose a wider original photograph.


A reusable brief for a product on a tabletop is: **Continue the pale stone tabletop to the left and right, with soft window light from the upper left. Keep the extra area simple, with open space for a headline. Do not add another product, text or logos.** This is a proposed prompt, not a promise that every instruction will be followed. Place the real headline and logo afterwards in a design editor.


In[Magic Hour’s full editor](https://magichour.ai/create/ai-image-expander) , upload the original, choose Custom, extend the required sides, and optionally enter the brief. Review the previewed expansion area and estimate before generating. If you need only a natural continuation, try leaving the optional prompt empty. The[step-by-step guide](https://help.magichour.ai/en/articles/16917119-ai-image-expander-step-by-step-guide) covers both paths.

## Fix the common problems before generating again


**The image did not expand:** check that the chosen canvas is larger than the source in at least one direction. In Custom, all-zero padding asks for no new area. In Photoroom, also inspect whether the background is a simple layer or a photographic scene.


**The scene gains duplicate products or odd furniture:** simplify the requested surroundings or reduce the expansion. Use the original subject as the fixed decision point; an attractive new scene is not enough if it changes what the image represents.


**The horizon or tabletop has a seam:** compare both sides of the boundary at 100% zoom. Try a smaller extension or finish the localized correction in an image editor rather than regenerating unrelated regions.


**Text or logos become unreliable:** preserve a source copy and add exact brand elements as separate layout assets. Do not rely on inferred lettering to reproduce packaging claims or a legal line.


**The ratio looks right but the image is too small:** check the actual downloaded dimensions and plan entitlement. Expansion controls composition; it does not by itself establish print resolution or the maximum size a tool can deliver.


## What to check before using an expanded image commercially


Separate three decisions: permission to process the source, the tool’s permission for the output, and whether the image truthfully represents the thing being sold. A paid license does not make an invented product feature accurate. Keep a source-to-output record for important campaign assets and check recognizable packaging, people and brand elements in the final composition.


For a single image, choose the workflow that gets it into the required layout with manageable cleanup. For repeated work, record accepted files, generations and export usage across the actual jobs. That gives you a useful operating cost without pretending that one vendor demonstration predicts your acceptance rate.
